# Currency safety audit (generated by scripts/safety_audit.py)

**All numbers below are offline, on SYNTHETIC or scan-derived images. They are not real-world accuracy.**

## 1. Deployed files and mapping

- model assets == runs/: **OK**
- labels assets == labels.json: **OK**
- thresholds assets == reports/: **OK**
- training class order == labels.json order: **OK**
- model input [1, 224, 224, 3] float32; output [1, 10] float32
- class order (index: id): 0:NEW_1, 1:NEW_2, 2:NEW_5, 3:NEW_10, 4:NEW_20, 5:OLD_1000, 6:OLD_2000, 7:OLD_5000, 8:OLD_10000, 9:NO_NOTE
- accept threshold tau = 0.98

## 4. Is the confidence calibrated?

Reliability = among predictions whose top probability falls in a bin, how often is the top class actually right. ECE = weighted mean |confidence - accuracy|. A score of 0.965 means 'the model is 96.5 % sure' ONLY if accuracy in that bin is also ~96.5 %.

**val** (n=750):

| top prob bin | n | mean confidence | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.000-0.500 | 17 | 0.407 | 0.059 |
| 0.500-0.700 | 43 | 0.593 | 0.372 |
| 0.700-0.900 | 47 | 0.825 | 0.617 |
| 0.900-0.965 | 55 | 0.942 | 0.891 |
| 0.965-0.990 | 81 | 0.979 | 0.963 |
| 0.990-1.000 | 507 | 0.998 | 1.000 |

ECE = 0.040

**test_sim** (n=700):

| top prob bin | n | mean confidence | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.500-0.700 | 6 | 0.600 | 0.500 |
| 0.700-0.900 | 12 | 0.847 | 0.917 |
| 0.900-0.965 | 25 | 0.932 | 1.000 |
| 0.965-0.990 | 57 | 0.980 | 1.000 |
| 0.990-1.000 | 600 | 0.999 | 1.000 |

ECE = 0.007

**test_collage** (n=200):

| top prob bin | n | mean confidence | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.000-0.500 | 8 | 0.411 | 0.375 |
| 0.500-0.700 | 19 | 0.604 | 0.737 |
| 0.700-0.900 | 15 | 0.814 | 0.867 |
| 0.900-0.965 | 22 | 0.935 | 0.955 |
| 0.965-0.990 | 26 | 0.980 | 0.923 |
| 0.990-1.000 | 110 | 0.998 | 1.000 |

ECE = 0.029

Reading: the model is trained to near-zero loss, so it is over-confident. Where accuracy in a bin is lower than the bin's confidence (see tables, especially the collage set) the score must NOT be read as a probability of being right.

## 5. How tau was chosen, and how sensitive it is

tau = smallest value where on VALIDATION: NO_NOTE falsely announced <= 1 % and wrong denomination <= 0.5 %. Validation is simulated from the same scans as training, so it cannot prove real-world safety; tau is a starting point only.

| tau | val: false note on NO_NOTE | val: wrong denomination | val: announced correctly | test-collage: wrong announced | test-collage: announced correctly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9 | 0.033 | 0.000 | 0.891 | 2/200 | 0.775 |
| 0.93 | 0.033 | 0.000 | 0.874 | 1/200 | 0.740 |
| 0.95 | 0.019 | 0.000 | 0.850 | 1/200 | 0.700 |
| 0.965 | 0.010 | 0.000 | 0.815 | 1/200 | 0.670 |
| 0.98 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.752 | 0/200 | 0.615 |
| 0.99 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.680 | 0/200 | 0.550 |
| 0.995 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.591 | 0/200 | 0.470 |

## 6. Unknown-input handling

- test_neg: n=300, argmax NO_NOTE 1.000, falsely announced a note **0**
- test_unsup: n=40, argmax NO_NOTE 0.900, falsely announced a note **0**
- The decider also treats NO_NOTE, NaN, wrong-size and non-probability outputs as 'no note' (unit tests `CurrencyDeciderTest`).
- NOT measured: hands holding paper, coloured cards, receipts, other countries' banknotes, screens showing notes - none exist in the data.

## 7. Sensitivity to the resize method

Each test-sim image was upscaled x4 and brought back to 224 with different filters (the app uses a 4-sample box average); argmax agreement with the original prediction:

- BOX: 0.990 (n=100)
- BILINEAR: 0.990 (n=100)
- LANCZOS: 1.000 (n=100)
- NEAREST: 1.000 (n=100)
